question.problem: The horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{7x-9{x}^{2}}{3{x}^{2}+8x-5}$ is $y=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

In this case, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{2}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{7x-9{x}^{2}}{3{x}^{2}+8x-5} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{7x}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{9{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}}+\frac{8x}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{7}{x}-9)}{(3+\frac{8}{x}-\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{7}{x},$ $\frac{8}{x},$ and $\frac{5}{{x}^{2}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(\frac{7}{x}-9)}{(3+\frac{8}{x}-\frac{5}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & \to \frac{0-9}{3+0-0} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=-3.$
